subject: Private vs Dedicated capacity mapping — MedSecure regulated workload sizing
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@medsecure.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@medsecure.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing ask: Private vs Dedicated for MedSecure regulated workloads

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MedSecure is moving quickly on a POC for our patient-facing inference (PHI scope). Procurement and infra need a side-by-side capacity and isolation comparison so leadership can choose between Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private (on our VPC / air-gapped option).

Top-level asks:
- Clear delta between Dedicated (hosted/reserved) and Private (customer VPC / on-prem) for throughput, latency, and operational constraints.
- Minimum viable GPU fleet to meet our expected peaks (we expect ~250 QPS peak for embedding + generation mix; tail latency SLO 300ms for short prompts).
- Security/compliance notes: KMS/HSM options, egress controls, SOC2 evidence we can point to.
- Procurement timeline: aiming for contract signature by end of July.

I've attached our high-level RFP outline to this thread. Can you produce a short decision worksheet and a recommended capacity estimate (ballpark) we can share with our infra team? If helpful, loop in your SE.

Attachments: MedSecure_RFP_outline.pdf

Thanks,
Anna Keller
CTO, MedSecure Analytics
anna.keller@medsecure.ai

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@medsecure.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: Private vs Dedicated for MedSecure regulated workloads

Anna — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. Looping Laura and Dev (SE + infra) to build a concise worksheet. Draft attached: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx.

High-level notes (quick):
- If you prioritize fastest time-to-value and predictable unit economics, Dedicated (reserved capacity) is the quicker path: we can provision an isolated GPU pool in our Dedicated tier with SLA-backed latency and no cross-tenant interference. For your 250 QPS mixed workload we estimate a starting Dedicated allocation of 6 x A100-80GB (serving quantized gpt-like models) with autoscaling buffer for bursts.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): provides the strongest isolation and full control over keys + egress but increases setup time (networking, air-gap validation) and ops cost. For on-prem H100-style hardware we'd recommend a minimum of 4 x H100 nodes to meet the 250 QPS target with headroom for KV cache warm-up and batch variability.
- Latency: Dedicated with NVLink-backed A100 pools should hit median <150ms for short prompts; Private depends on your internal NIC topology — add ~20-40ms if traffic crosses datacenter boundaries.
- Ops/Compliance: Private gives you full KMS control, but Redwood Private can also be integrated with customer-managed KMS and tight audit logs. We'll attach SOC2 evidence checklist next.

Open items where we need your input to firm up estimates:
1) Typical prompt lengths / token distribution (short chat vs long-document generation).
2) Percentage of requests requiring embeddings or long-context generation (these change memory footprint).
3) Whether you require absolute zero egress for PHI paths or if referential telemetry (metrics only) is OK.

Next steps: Laura / Dev — can you validate the ballpark in the sheet and add per-option tradeoffs (cost, time-to-deploy, operational complexity)?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Attachment: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, Anna Keller <anna.keller@medsecure.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: Private vs Dedicated for MedSecure regulated workloads

Anna / Sergio — quick SE note with technical tradeoffs and conservative numbers. Attaching SOC2 evidence checklist for procurement.

Summary bullets (technical):
- Workload profile assumptions: 60% short chat (<=128 tokens), 30% embeddings (384-dim), 10% long generation (>=2k tokens). If your distribution shifts, we need to re-run the sizing.
- Dedicated option (hosted, reserved pool):
  - Starting fleet: 6 x NVIDIA A100-80GB (quantized FP16/INT8 where applicable) with continuous batching and prefix caching.
  - Expected P50 generation latency: ~120-160ms; P95 depending on batch windows ~300-450ms unless you tighten SLOs and reduce batching.
  - Time-to-prod: ~2–4 weeks (contract + capacity provisioning + integration).
  - Benefits: faster ops, Redwood-managed patching, integrated metrics, and can be isolated by tenant/VPC peering for restricted comms.
- Private option (customer VPC / on-prem):
  - Minimum hardware: 4 x H100 or equivalent (if you need sustained long-context with large batch throughput consider 6 nodes).
  - Considerations: network topology (RDMA), storage locality for KV cache, and KMS integration. Setup time ~6–10 weeks for air-gapped/on-prem validation.
  - Benefits: full control over keys, zero external egress (if required), and can meet strict regulatory policies.
- Hybrid approach: Dedicated reserved capacity for general traffic + Private endpoints for PHI-only paths. This reduces cost/time while meeting isolation requirements.

Compliance notes: see SOC2 checklist; Redwood can provide audit logs and can integrate with customer HSM. For "no-external-egress" requirements we'll need to map which API endpoints must be routed to Private only; label them in the MAA.

I'll update the capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx with a tab for the hybrid option and add cost multipliers. Also attached SOC2_evidence_checklist.pdf per procurement.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Attachment: SOC2_evidence_checklist.pdf

From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@medsecure.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@medsecure.ai, jonathan.hayes@cloudvendor.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: Private vs Dedicated for MedSecure regulated workloads

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from infra/procurement:
- Zero-external-egress is required for PHI endpoints (we will run a small subset of endpoints that handle PHI). Non-PHI telemetry/metrics may be OK to route to hosted Dedicated.
- QPS profile: sustained 120 QPS with 250 QPS peak bursts (bursts ~5–10 minutes), mostly short prompts but embeddings are frequent.
- Key management: we require customer-controlled KMS for PHI path (HSM preferred).
- Procurement timeline is firm: legal kicks off next week and we need an MAA + SOW draft this sprint.

Can you include a short canary plan for the hybrid option (how we route PHI traffic to Private endpoints first then failover to Dedicated + alerts)? Also please add a ballpark monthly run-rate for each option (Dedicated-only, Private-only, Hybrid) in the updated sheet so procurement has a cost comparator.

Anna

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@medsecure.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: Private vs Dedicated for MedSecure regulated workloads

Anna — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a short decision worksheet and MAA draft (MAA_draft.docx) plus updated capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (hybrid tab + cost rows). Summary below to share with legal/procurement: 

Executive summary (two recommended options):
1) Hybrid (recommended for speed + compliance):
   - Architecture: Dedicated reserved pool handles non-PHI traffic; PHI endpoints routed to Private VPC/air-gapped deployment.
   - Minimum capacity: Dedicated: 4 x A100 (handles non-PHI at 120 sustained QPS with autoscale headroom); Private: 3 x H100 (handles PHI burst capability).
   - Expected time-to-live (TTL) to prod: 4–6 weeks (parallel workstreams for contract and Private setup).
   - Ballpark run-rate: ~USD 120k–160k/month (combined; depends on commitment level and node types).
2) Private-only (strongest isolation):
   - Minimum capacity: 6 x H100 (sustained 250 QPS with long-context workloads).
   - Time to deploy: 8–12 weeks (on-prem validations + audit).
   - Ballpark run-rate: ~USD 200k+/month (CAPEX or reserved managed private).

Canary / rollout plan (hybrid):
- Phase 0: Provision Dedicated pool and deploy non-PHI routes. Smoke tests and latency verification (>7 days).
- Phase 1: Stand up Private PHI nodes in your VPC, enable mutual TLS and customer KMS. Run mirrored traffic (shadow) for 48–72 hours.
- Phase 2: Route 5% PHI traffic to Private, monitor P50/P95 and error rates for 3–5 days.
- Phase 3: Increase to 50% then 100% after sign-off; keep automatic fallback to Dedicated with alerting if Private SLOs breach.

Action items:
- Sergio: schedule SE workshop this week (I will send a calendar invite).
- Anna/procurement: share tokenized prompt samples and final list of PHI endpoints to label in the MAA.
- Legal: we will push a draft MAA + SOW; please expect DocuSign link in ~48 hours.

I'll follow up with the updated attachments and a short one-page decision worksheet for leadership. Happy to jump on a call with infra and procurement tomorrow.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Attachments: MAA_draft.docx, capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx
